details: Hackers exploited a firmware flaw in Coldcard hardware wallets, draining approximately $88.6 million in Bitcoin from over 4,500 addresses. The ongoing attack has reignited debate over the safety of self-custody, with a Bloomberg analyst suggesting it strengthens the case for regulated spot Bitcoin ETFs as a safer alternative. Transfers of small Bitcoin amounts surged to levels not seen since the FTX collapse as users moved funds.
title: Coldcard Wallet Hack Drains $88.6M in Bitcoin; Fuels ETF Debate

details: A Reuters investigation revealed an unlicensed Dubai-based crypto exchange, Shelbit, facilitated over $4 billion in Iranian sanctions evasion since May 2024. The illicit network involved illegal gambling, Iranian Bitcoin mining, and direct financial links to Iran's central bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Dubai regulators have since ordered Shelbit to cease its unlicensed activity.
title: Iran Used Dubai Crypto Exchange Shelbit for $4B Sanctions Evasion

details: The CLARITY Act, a bill aiming to classify XRP as a commodity, faces an uncertain future in the Senate, with only five working days remaining before recess for a floor vote. Its passage, considered crucial for attracting institutional investment into XRP, is hampered by ongoing disputes over stablecoin rules and ethics provisions concerning officials' crypto profits. Polymarket currently estimates only a 30% chance of the bill passing in 2026.
title: CLARITY Act Faces Senate Hurdles, Lowers XRP's Near-Term Outlook

details: Bitmine Immersion Technologies announced its total crypto and cash holdings reached $11.3 billion as of August 2, including 5.8 million Ethereum (ETH) tokens, representing 4.8% of the total ETH supply. The company highlighted that Ethereum significantly outperformed the Nasdaq 100 index in July, reflecting strengthening crypto fundamentals. Bitmine also repurchased 4.5 million shares of its common stock.
title: Bitmine Reports $11.3B Crypto Holdings, ETH Outperforms Nasdaq 100

details: South Africa's National Treasury and Reserve Bank have released draft guidelines for cross-border cryptocurrency transactions, aiming to integrate digital assets into its financial control framework. The proposed rules would require all such transfers to pass through authorized service providers and be reported to the central bank. The draft also suggests that South African companies could face a ban on cross-border crypto activities, while individuals would be limited by existing foreign currency allowances.
title: South Africa Proposes Strict Rules for Cross-Border Crypto Transfers

details: Bitcoin futures yields have consistently underperformed benchmark US Treasury notes since February 2026. Currently, Bitcoin futures return around 3%, compared to an average of 3.8% for two-year Treasuries. This collapse in yield impacts traditional carry trades, reducing the incentive for traders to deploy capital into Bitcoin futures and contributing to a slowdown in futures market activity.
title: Bitcoin Futures Yields Drop Below US Treasuries, Hurting Carry Trades

details: American Bitcoin (ABTC), a firm backed by the Trump brothers, reported a Q2 net loss of $57.2 million despite achieving record quarterly mining production of 932 BTC and increasing its Bitcoin holdings by 14% to over 8,000 BTC. The loss was primarily attributed to an unrealized fair-value loss of $71.2 million on its digital assets, compounded by Bitcoin's 11% price decline during the quarter.
title: Trump-Backed American Bitcoin Reports Q2 Loss Amid BTC Price Slide

details: Stablecoin issuer Circle has acquired nearly 1,000 blockchain patents from IBM, encompassing over 680 patent families across various sectors including blockchain technology, banking, and enterprise infrastructure. This strategic acquisition positions Circle as the leading US holder of blockchain patents, aiming to bolster its USDC stablecoin and other on-chain products for internet-native finance.
title: Circle Acquires IBM's Blockchain Patent Portfolio, Becomes Top US Holder

details: Swiss digital asset bank AMINA (formerly SEBA Bank), a FINMA-regulated institution, is collaborating with Wall Street firm Cantor Fitzgerald to explore options for a public listing. The bank's immediate focus is on raising strategic growth capital, with a reverse merger via a digital asset treasury company being a preferred route, though no final decision has been made.
title: Swiss Crypto Bank AMINA Explores Public Listing with Cantor Fitzgerald
